title: Dry Scalp and Oily Hair: Why It Happens and How to Fix It
summary: Key Takeaways Dry scalp and oily hair can happen at the same time. A compromised scalp moisture barrier can leave your scalp feeling dry while sebaceous glands continue producing oil. Oil and moisture are not the same thing. Your scalp may produce excess oil, but your hair lengths and ends can still lack hydration and become dry. Hair type influences how oil travels. Straight hair tends to look oilier because sebum moves easily down the hair shaft, while curly and coily hair often experiences drier lengths and ends. Overwashing can contribute to oily roots. Frequent shampooing may disrupt the scalp's natural balance and encourage increased oil production over time. The right routine supports balance. Lightweight hydration, weekly hair masks, gentle cleansing, and personalized products can help create a healthier balance between scalp comfort, moisture retention, and oil control.
